RAG stands for Retrieval Augmented Generation, a technique that grounds LLM outputs in external knowledge.
In RAG, a retriever fetches relevant documents from a corpus, and a generator uses them to produce an answer.
Vector embeddings map text into dense numerical representations where semantic similarity corresponds to geometric proximity.
FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is a library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors.
Sentence-Transformers produce fixed-size embeddings by pooling transformer outputs, commonly using mean pooling.
The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model is a lightweight sentence embedding model with 384-dimensional output.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors regardless of magnitude, making it useful for semantic search.
L2 (Euclidean) distance measures the straight-line distance between two points in embedding space.
Chunking strategies for RAG include fixed-size chunks, sentence splitting, and recursive character splitting.
Overlap between chunks helps preserve context that might be lost at chunk boundaries.
Transformers are neural network architectures based on self-attention mechanisms, introduced in the 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need.
BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) is a pre-trained language model for understanding tasks.
GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) is an autoregressive model designed for text generation.
T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer) frames every NLP task as a text-to-text problem.
The Flan-T5 model family are instruction-tuned versions of T5 that perform better on zero-shot tasks.
Hugging Face Transformers is an open-source library providing thousands of pre-trained models for NLP, vision, and audio.
Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model to a specific downstream task using a smaller labeled dataset.
Transfer learning leverages knowledge from one task or domain to improve performance on another.
Prompt engineering involves crafting effective instructions to guide LLM behavior without changing model weights.
Few-shot prompting provides examples in the prompt to help the model understand the desired output format.
Chain-of-thought prompting encourages the model to reason step-by-step before giving a final answer.
Agentic AI systems can plan, use tools, and iteratively refine their outputs to complete complex tasks.
In an agentic loop, the model follows a cycle of Plan, Act, Observe, and Reflect.
Tool-augmented LLMs can call external functions like calculators, search engines, and databases.
ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) is a paradigm where the model interleaves reasoning traces with actions.
Self-reflection allows an agent to review and correct its own outputs before returning them to the user.
Hallucination in LLMs refers to generating plausible-sounding but factually incorrect information.
Grounding LLM outputs in retrieved evidence is a primary strategy for reducing hallucinations.
FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building APIs, featuring automatic OpenAPI documentation.
Pydantic provides data validation and settings management using Python type annotations.
Uvicorn is a lightning-fast ASGI server for running Python web applications.
REST (Representational State Transfer) APIs use HTTP methods to perform CRUD operations on resources.
Docker containers package applications with their dependencies for consistent deployment across environments.
CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment) automates testing and deployment workflows.
Unit tests verify individual components in isolation, while integration tests check component interactions.
pytest is a popular Python testing framework that supports fixtures, parametrization, and plugins.
Python virtual environments (venv) isolate project dependencies from the system Python installation.
pip is the standard package installer for Python, reading dependencies from requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.
NumPy provides efficient array operations and is the foundation of the Python numerical computing stack.
Natural Language Processing (NLP) encompasses tasks like classification, generation, translation, and summarization.
Tokenization splits text into subword units that language models can process.
Attention mechanisms allow models to focus on relevant parts of the input when producing each output token.
Word2Vec and GloVe are older embedding techniques that produce static word vectors.
Contextual embeddings from transformer models capture meaning that varies based on surrounding words.
Information retrieval (IR) is the science of searching for documents that satisfy an information need.
BM25 is a classical term-frequency based ranking function still used as a baseline in modern IR systems.
Hybrid search combines dense vector retrieval with sparse keyword matching for improved recall.
Cross-encoder models score query-document pairs jointly, providing more accurate but slower relevance judgments.
Re-ranking uses a more expensive model to re-order the top candidates from a fast first-stage retriever.
Knowledge graphs represent facts as entities and relationships, complementing unstructured text retrieval.
Embedding dimension, index type, and search parameters all affect the speed-accuracy trade-off in vector search.
Quantization reduces embedding precision (e.g., float32 to int8) to cut memory usage and speed up search.
Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms like HNSW and IVF trade small accuracy losses for large speed gains.
Python is a versatile programming language widely used in data science, web development, and AI research.
VS Code is a free source code editor made by Microsoft with extensive extension support.
Git is a distributed version control system used to track changes in source code during development.
GitHub provides cloud-based Git hosting along with features like pull requests, issues, and Actions CI/CD.
